teaser.en: Green above, silver below: the Digo know this Croton by the two colours of its leaves.

summary.en: Mtsunduzi is Croton megalocarpoides, a shrub or small tree of the dry coastal country. Pakia gives it as one of the few plants the Digo identify by leaf colour.

about.en: Mtsunduzi is a shrub or small tree up to about 8 m, with grey bark that cracks into rectangular scales. Its leaves are green above and silvery beneath. Digo people describe this as 'ndani n’maru, konze n’mereru', green on the upper surface and whitish on the lower. Its fruits are three-lobed capsules, as in other crotons.

where.en: It grows in dry coastal bushland and forest from southern Somalia to Mozambique, in Kenya from near sea level to about 275 m.

culture.en: Pakia notes that Digo plant description uses only three basic colour words, nyiru, nyereru and kundu, so colour seldom separates species. Mtsunduzi is one of the exceptions: its two-toned leaves make it identifiable on sight.

names.en: Pakia records the Digo name Mtsunduzi but gives no meaning or shared names. Its scientific name is Croton megalocarpoides.

reason.en: Another member of the spurge family
